records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?

Honestly? I'd have said more. Earlier. To all of you.

I'm not great at letting people in and out here it wasn't any different. I kept things close to my chest when I probably should've just put them out there.

I'd have talked to you about the bottle the same day it happened instead of letting it sit. Not to embarrass you, just to deal with it before it had a chance to grow into something worse. I let that go too long.

He needed somebody to just be present with him more than he needed to collect wood. I knew that and I still kept defaulting back to the task list.

I think I'd also have told DaVinci what he meant to the group more. He kept everybody moving when the rest of us were dragging and I don't think I ever actually said that to him out loud.

records.response_pred: Honestly? If I had to do it over, I think I'd have said something sooner when things started to go wrong. Maybe we could've avoided some of the problems we had, but it's hard to say. I did my best with what I knew at the time, and we made it through.

records.response_truth:
None. They didn't serve any practical purpose at all.

I think you understand that more than you're letting on. You asked the question at the end of your notebook. You didn't have to write that. It didn't help the resource log. But you wrote it anyway.

That's your flowers, Donatello.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
